newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea says will return N.Korean bodies if asked.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea says will return N.Korean bodies if asked.

text.p: South Korea will return the bodies of North Koreans shot dead after landing from a submarine in September if Pyongyang makes a request, the defence ministry said on Monday.

Earlier, the United Nations Command said it may conduct a "repatriation of remains" ceremony on Monday afternoon. The move comes a day after Pyongyang apologised for the incursion of the submarine that set ashore 26 infiltrators. Twenty four of the intruders were killed.

"Since North Korea has officially apologised and promised to prevent a recurrence of such incidents we have decided to return the bodies through appropriate channels if North Korea makes a request," a defence ministry statement said.
"We look forward to North Korea's cooperation towards peace and stability on the Korean peninsula."
The U.S.-led United Nations Command monitors a ceasefire that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
The bodies would be sent home via the border crossing point of Panmunjom.
